correctness.rationale: The source supplies both pullback identities pi^*omega_X^{-1}=O_H(1) and pi^*A=O_H(1), so the norm for the degree-two finite flat map gives A^2=omega_X^{-2}. The local generator in Proposition 4.5 identifies A^2 with the degree-two D-invariants. The global kernel computation is exact: D(q)=ell Q+mu C, t^3 and x_i t^2 coefficients force ell=0, D(B)=C reduces to the polynomial kernel, and that kernel consists precisely of seven squares. They are independent modulo Q. Their common zero set is empty, yielding basepoint-freeness. The pulled-back map is relative Frobenius on the integral fourfold H, of degree 16; division by deg(pi)=2 gives the purely inseparable degree 8 map from X. The source sheaf injection then gives seven independent one-forms.

value.rationale: The complete bi-anticanonical system is a basic birational invariant of a Fano variety, and this example is the first known smooth irregular Fano fourfold. Determining that the system has seven sections and is a finite purely inseparable degree-eight map onto the Frobenius twist of the original complete intersection gives a concrete projective model for X and sharpens the known differential-form lower bound from six to seven. This is structural geometry of the extremal example, not a routine recomputation or arbitrary finite slice.
